Independent product-metric prefix enumeration on path and star products for factors d=2,3,4; verified pairwise Lipschitz inequalities for all prefixes in five finite profiles.
correctness.rationale: For d>=1 nontrivial finite unit-edge trees, product shortest-path metric, arbitrary roots, commuting prefix retractions have exact optimum 1 for one or two factors and 2 for three or more. For one factor parent folds are nonexpansive. For two factors, lex parent-before-descendant order and simultaneous coordinate-parent predecessor make each one-point fold nonexpansive on prior prefix: when earlier first coordinate differs it is outside current descendant subtree so first coordinate distance drops by one, compensating second coordinate; within same first row the second-coordinate parent distance drops. For d>=3 recursive row-prefix maps use ancestral projections π_Q in the first factor, change by at most one in that coordinate when second-factor membership changes, making graph-edge output distance<=2. Nested one-point fold compositions commute. For lower bound, any last vertex v has three neighbors in distinct factors whose closed radius-one balls intersect only at v; penultimate retraction must move v but fix its neighbors, so integer Lipschitz <2 is impossible. The result is about retractional free-space projections, not arbitrary Banach bases.
residual_risks: Tree edges must have unit length, and singleton factors are excluded/omitted.
Recursive construction requires parent-before-descendant orders; a generic vertex lex order with arbitrary parent assignments would not suffice.

evidence: Novotný circles are not products of tree metrics, and the paper concerns different obstructions.
